props.title: Django
props.initialSlug: Lone gunslinger seeks revenge in brutal spaghetti west

sections.content: Django revolutionized Spaghetti Westerns with Franco Nero's mud-caked, coffin-dragging antihero. Director Sergio Corbucci crafted a brutally violent response to Sergio Leone's A Fistful of Dollars (1964), pushing the genre into darker territory. The film's striking opening sequence - Django dragging a mysterious coffin through muddy wasteland - instantly became iconic, inspiring over 30 unofficial sequels and directly influencing Quentin Tarantino's Django Unchained (2012). Corbucci's unflinching depiction of violence, particularly the ear-cutting scene, established new boundaries for on-screen brutality in Westerns.

sections.content: Django's influence rippled through Italian cinema, spawning countless imitators. Keoma (1976) starring Franco Nero reimagined the character in a post-apocalyptic setting, while Django Kill... If You Live, Shoot! (1967) took the formula into surreal, hallucinatory territory. The film's success helped establish the "lone gunslinger" archetype that dominated European Westerns, visible in later works like Day of Anger (1967) and The Big Gundown (1966).

Technically, Django broke new ground with Luis Bacalov's haunting title song and Giuseppe Ruzzolini's mud-caked cinematography. The film's use of extreme close-ups and dramatic zooms became hallmarks of the Spaghetti Western style, while its political undertones - addressing racism and revolutionary politics - distinguished it from American Westerns of the era like The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966). sections.content: Django's influence extends far beyond Westerns. The character's black-clad appearance inspired Japanese manga and countless video games. The film's brutal violence and moral ambiguity paved the way for revisionist Westerns like The Wild Bunch (1969) and modern neo-Westerns such as No Country for Old Men (2007). Even the coffin-as-weapon concept has been repeatedly borrowed, appearing in everything from Desperado (1995) to various anime series.
